City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
January 3, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on January 3, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on December 23, 2011, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
W. Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
William P. Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness
INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and Cityâ??s Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City Manager.) The Cityâ??s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
CS2.
Conference with Real Property Negotiator pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.8. Property is an approximate 7.126 acre Site, APN 761-072-01 with a common street address of 26742 Oso Parkway, Mission Viejo, California owned by Mission Viejo Oso Parkway Development, LP, a California limited partnership (also known as "Watermarke" or "Andalucia Apartments"). Housing Authority negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager/Housing Authority Executive Director, Charles Wilson, Director of Community Development, James Williams, Economic Advisor, Celeste Brady, Housing Authority Counsel, William P. Curley III, City Attorney. Owner's negotiators: Greg Neville of Watermarke and counsel Jeffrey Oderman of Rutan & Tucker. Under negotiation: potential acquisition real property interest, a deed of trust that secures long term affordable housing and the price and terms therefor related to the above-listed property. Factors affecting price and terms under negotiation: recorded covenants and affordable housing requirements to implement City's Housing Element of the General Plan relating to housing opportunity Site B. Factors affecting time of payment: conditions to closing, due diligence, and schedule of development and completion of the affordable housing project.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session Item CS1 the Council provided general direction for staff follow-up and he anticipates that a final agreement will be brought to the Council for consideration at the next meeting.
For item CS2, Mr. Curley and Special Counsel Celeste Brady provided information on the California Supreme Court’s recent decision to invalidate Assembly Bill 1X 27 which would have allowed redevelopment agencies to continue to operate, subject to new restrictions and limitations. Due to the ruling, Ms. Brady indicated that the City’s Community Development Agency will be dissolved and she will provide a lengthier presentation at an upcoming Council Meeting.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Presentation to Former Mayor Leckness
Mayor Ury presented a gavel plaque to Council Member Leckness in recognition of his service as Mayor in 2011.
P2.
Opening Remarks from Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury presented his opening remarks and his goals for the year.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Larry Mauer, M.V.: invited the Council and residents to a concert featuring the music of George Gershwin, on January 26, 2012, from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. in the City Council Chamber. Natassia and Neal Smith: stated that they are the new owners of the Quiznos on Jeronimo Road and they wished to thank the Council and the community for donating items and helping with their first "Quizmas" which benefited the South County Outreach and the Mission Viejo YMCA. Dan Avery, M.V.: discussed the distinction between condoning sexual offenders and protecting the constitution. Larry Gilbert, M.V.: commented on the Supreme Court’s recent ruling regarding AB 1X 27 and he expressed concern that the City has promised the builders at UDR and Watermarke millions of dollars in redevelopment monies. Don Asay, M.V.: on behalf of the Mission Viejo Activities Committee, he thanked the Council for their support of the annual Santa’s Arrival event and Santa’s Workshop. He further thanked the members of the Activities Committee and the residents of Mission Viejo for participating in this extremely successful event.
Steve Magdziak, M.V.: stated that the amendments to the Brown Act didn’t make it stronger, they made it weaker. He believes in the original intent of the law and he announced that he doesn’t agree with discussing labor negotiations in Closed Sessions.
Robert D. Breton, M.V.: expressed his support and gave thanks for the wonderful things that have happened in Mission Viejo this last year. He stated that the arts are flourishing in Mission Viejo, thanks to the Council and city staff.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 2, 11, 13, and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
3.
Check Register dated November 25, 2011 in the amount of $869,716.44
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated December 2, 2011 in the amount of $1,201,474.50
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Check Register dated December 9, 2011 in the amount of $987,955.14
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
City Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2011
Received and filed.
7.
Community Development Agency (CDA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2011
Received and filed.
8.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2011
Received and filed.
9.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for October 2011
Received and filed.
10.
Delegation of Authority to Request Disbursements from the Other Post Employment Prefunding Plan
Adopted Resolution 12-01 Approving the Delegation of Authority to Request Disbursements from Other Post Employment Prefunding Plan.
12.
Mission Viejo Library Story Time Room Remodel (CIP 601)
(1) Rejected all bids for the project; and (2) authorized staff to re-advertise for "remodeling" bids for the subject project.
14.
Traffic Signal Maintenance Contract
(1) Awarded the contract for the subject services to Republic ITS for the period from January 1, 2012, through June 30, 2013, in the amount of $637,500; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Republic ITS for the period from January 1, 2012, through June 30, 2012, in an amount not to exceed $212,500.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
11.
Ordinance Regarding Sex Offenders in City Parks and Recreation Facilities
City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.
Tony Rackauckas, Orange County District Attorney: expressed his support for the proposed ordinance and discussed the history of the County’s ordinance on the same subject.
Larry Gilbert, M.V.: expressed concern that this item was listed on the Consent Calendar and thanked the Distict Attorney for presenting the idea, and Council Member Schlicht for bringing it forward and putting it on the agenda.
Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to introduce Ordinance 12-292 Adding a New Chapter 11.23 of Title 11 To The Mission Viejo Municipal Code Prohibiting Registered Sex Offenders From Entering City Parks And Recreation Facilities.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
16.
Presentation by Colby Durnin of Kaleidoscope Regarding the Improvements that have been made since Acquisition and their Conceptual Plans for the Next Phase of the Project's Redevelopment
The City Council received a presentation from Colby Durnin regarding recent and proposed improvements to the Kaleidoscope center. In addition he discussed proposed signage for the exterior of the building and the entrances.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to refer this matter to the Planning and Transportation Commission and direct staff to present options for creating a sign district for Kaleidoscope and possibly a larger area.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
Council Member Schlicht noted for the record that she is opposed to special district signage because she thinks it is business unfriendly to the rest of the community and she is also opposed to 20’x60’ electronic signs.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)
2.
City Council Minutes
Council Member Schlicht asked that the Minutes be amended to include her question to the City Attorney regarding the legitimacy of the Closed Session for discussion of the Assistant City Manager’s contract, and also the City Attorney’s response.
Mayor Ury requested that the Minutes also reflect that all five Council Members participated in the Closed Session.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of December 5, 2011, as amended (amendments described above.)
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
13.
Via Fabricante and Peter A. Hartman Way Intersection Modifications
Council Member Schlicht requested that the red light at the intersection remain green until activated by a pedestrian. Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon noted that the proposal is for stop signs, not a traffic signal.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon asked for a brief history on the SVUSD and the changes that they made to accommodate the special needs children. She wondered why the classrooms could not be contained to one side of the street.
Mr. Chagnon stated that he is not aware of the school district's process in determining the location of the classrooms and City Manager Wilberg noted that the City adjusts and cooperates with the school districts to address the changing needs that they face.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution 12-02 Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Modify the Intersection of Via Fabricante and Peter A. Hartman Way into a Multi-Way, Stop-Controlled Intersection with a Designated Striped Crosswalk in the City of Mission Viejo as Shown on the Attached Exhibit A.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
15.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report and provided a history on the change orders and the problems that the contractor has faced at the construction site.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to Direct (1) Approve Change Order No. 3 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in the amount of $48,542.45; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-XX Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project 501 for $51,935.00.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
RECESS
At the hour of 8:20 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:34 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
MAYOR'S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
17.
Investment Advisory Commission and Planning and Transportation Commission Vacancies
By consensus, the City Council (1) declared the vacancy of Investment Advisory Commissioner Dominic Nolan, (2) declared the upcoming vacancy of Planning and Transportation Commissioner Rick Sandzimier, and (3) directed the City Clerk to post the notice of unscheduled vacancy.
18.
City Council Committee and Regional Board/Committee Representative Appointments
(1) Mayor Ury appointed representatives and alternates to the following regional boards/committees as follows:
Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors (by adoption of Resolution 12-04 ): Representative - Council Member Kelley.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES: Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
NOES: Schlicht
ABSTAIN: Kelley
ABSENT: None
Orange County Fire Authority Board of Directors (by adoption of Resolution 12-04 ): Alternate - Council Member Leckness.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote: AYES: Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES: None
ABSTAIN: Leckness
ABSENT: None Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency: Representative – Mayor Ury.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES: Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES: None
ABSTAIN: Ury
ABSENT: None
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency: Alternate – Council Member Leckness.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES: Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES: None
ABSTAIN: Leckness
ABSENT: None
Orange County Vector Control District – No appointment made. Directed the City Clerk to advertise the vacancy and seek resident volunteers with experience in vector control.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency: Representative – Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES: Kelley, Leckness, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES: None
ABSTAIN: Reardon
ABSENT: None
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency: Alternate – Council Member Kelley.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES: Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES: None
ABSTAIN: Kelley
ABSENT: None
(2) By consensus, the City Council formed a Standing Economic Development Committee and Mayor Ury appointed Council Member Leckness and Council Member Kelley to serve on the Committee. Mayor Ury requested that the Committee provide the Council with reports in 90 days and in 6 months.
(3) Mayor Ury appointed members/alternates to the existing City of Mission Viejo ad hoc committees as follows:
(a) CUSD Ad Hoc Committee: Representative – Council Member Kelley, Alternate - Council Member Leckness.
(b) CDA RFP Site C Ad Hoc Committee: Representative – Council Member Schlicht, Alternate - Council Member Kelley.
(4) Mayor Ury appointed representatives and alternates to the following regional boards/committees as follows:
(a) California Joint Powers Insurance Authority – Council Member Schlicht/Director of Admin Services Cheryl Dyas.
(b) League of California Cities and Association of California Cities, Orange County (*Representatives to the League are Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem – Mayor Ury/Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
(c) South Orange County Major Investment Study (SOCMIS) Policy Working Group - Committee is inactive (no appointments.)
(d) Measure M Growth Management Area 9 and 10 Interjurisdictional Forum - Committee is inactive (no appointments.)
(e) Orange County Council of Governments General Assembly – Council Member Schlicht/Mayor Ury.
(f) Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) General Assembly – Council Member Kelley/Mayor Ury.
(g) Southern Orange County Watershed Management Area Executive Committee – Mayor Pro Tem Reardon/Council Member Schlicht.
(h) Transportation Corridor System (TCS) – Mayor Ury/Mayor Pro Tem Reardon.
19.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley stated that there has not been a regular meeting of the OCFA Board since her last report however she presented a report on the December 7, 2011, special meeting of the OCFA Executive Committee.
20.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA therefore he had nothing to report.
21.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Council Member Leckness announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin Hills TCA.
22.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the SCAG TCC so she has nothing to report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
23.
Digital Recording and Online Availability of Commission Meetings
Mayor Ury and City Manager Wilberg reported that staff will begin digitally recording the Council and Commission meetings and those recordings will be available on line at the end of the month or in early February.
City Attorney’s Report
City Attorney Curley announced that he had nothing to report.
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
24.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
Receive reports.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley stated that it was a fun December and she heard numerous comments on the beautiful holiday lighting which really makes an impression on the residents. She enjoyed taking her grandchildren to visit Santa in his workshop and she stated that it was another huge success. Council Member Kelley thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee and the City staff who work to make sure that we have a safe, beautiful and fun experience for the children of the community. Council Member Kelley also announced that she enjoyed attending the opening of Mission Viejo Christian School’s new campus at the former O’Neill Elementary School site. She is very excited about Mission Viejo Christian School moving to that campus and the staff and principal could not be more pleased. There is room for growth and the neighbors will be delighted that there is a top-notch school back in the neighborhood. Lastly, Council Member Kelley noted that the Community of Character word for the month of January is perseverance.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness stated that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee holiday “Clark Griswold” lighting award went to the residents of Via Amistoso who outdid themselves. The whole cul-de-sac was lit up and he enjoyed visiting on several occasions and seeing the cars lined up on the street with occupants waiting to enjoy the fantastic lights and decorations.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht assured the residents that it has been her honor and privilege to represent the community values at the dais for the past year and she looks forward to continuing to do that. She agreed that it is the Council’s job to preserve and enhance the beauty of the community and she will continue to do that. Council Member Schlicht expressed her concern about the potential for 20x60’ signs at Kaleidoscope. She wished the residents a very happy, healthy and prosperous New Year.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon thanked her colleagues for electing her to serve as Mayor Pro Tem and she stated that she is looking forward to a really good year. She also thanked Mayor Ury for appointing her to the 73 Toll Road Board of Directors. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that since the last Council Meeting, she enjoyed meeting with several constituents and also with Colby Durnin of Kaleidoscope regarding the proposed upgrades and signage at the center. She believes that something needs to be done because the signage is not looking good now. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon also had the great pleasure of hearing the Mission Viejo Christian School Kids Club sing Christmas carols at city hall on December 23 and, earlier today, she enjoyed attending the opening of the school’s new campus. They have done a beautiful job renovating the former O’Neill school property and she encouraged residents to visit. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon discussed the Marguerite Tennis Center change orders and she expressed her appreciation that staff brought a change order to the Council tonight, before the work has been done. She stated that she could stand by on the sidelines and criticize the tennis center because she did not vote to approve the project in its entirety but she will not do that. Instead, she wants the project to be run well and to go smoothly and therefore she appreciates staff coming to the Council with new information on the project. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon reminded residents to pray for young Cade Spinello. January 15, 2012, is the one-year anniversary since his stroke and she was pleased to report that Cade is making vast strides and improvements.
Mayor Ury
25.
"Improve Don’t Move" Program
Mayor Ury presented his report.
Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: expressed support for the program and stated that it will not only help property owners but enhanced curb appeal will also help the neighborhoods. Further, it can help local contractors gain new business.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to authorize necessary budget adjustments in the amount of $360,000.00 to waive home improvement building permit fees for Mission Viejo homeowners from January 1, 2012, to July 4, 2012, and waive penalties for homeowners who bring previously non-inspected improvements into compliance.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Mayor Ury announced that he had a conversation with a Council Member from a neighboring city who was very impressed with Mission Viejo’s holiday lighting along La Paz Road, and he thanked staff for doing an outstanding job. He also thanked Council Member Leckness for doing a wonderful job as Mayor last year. He noted that Dave Leckness set a new standard for the Council to work towards and it was a very fun year. Mayor Ury announced that any future changes to the Tennis Center project will be placed on the Old Business agenda. He concluded his comments by thanking the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for all their hard work during the holidays and he wished everyone a Happy New Year.
ADJOURN
At the hour of 9:35 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adourned the meeting to Monday, January 16, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of January 16, 2012
